notes: DRAFT for scholarly review; nothing here is reviewed or published. English only: Arabic and Urdu texts are left null for translators. Written from the Quran text in content/quran (Tanzil Uthmani) in the drafter's own words; no published translation is quoted. Quran only: no hadith, no tafsir, no later tradition in the story texts. The occasions of revelation (who the persons were, what happened) are not in the verses; they appear only under unknowns and uncertainties, as later tradition, with the hadith to add later. Pronouns the Arabic leaves open are left open. Chapters are a reading order, not a chronology. Honorifics are added when the page is rendered.

claims.statement_en: The passage tells that someone frowned and turned away because the blind man came to him.
The verse asks the one addressed what would let him know: perhaps the blind man might purify himself.
He might also be reminded, and the reminder would benefit him.
As for the one who considers himself in no need, the one addressed attends to him.
It is not upon the one addressed if that one does not purify himself.
As for the one who came to the one addressed striving, and he fears, the one addressed is distracted from him.

chapters.summary_md: The passage tells that someone frowned and turned away because the blind man came to him [c1]. It says that the blind man might purify himself or be reminded, and the reminder would benefit him [c2][c3]. It speaks of the one who came striving, and fears, and from whom attention was turned [c6].
chapters.body_md:
The passage tells that someone frowned and turned away because the blind man came to him [c1].

The verse then asks the one addressed what would let him know: perhaps the blind man might purify himself [c2], or he might be reminded, and the reminder would benefit him [c3].

As for the one who considers himself in no need, the one addressed attends to him [c4]. It is not upon the one addressed if that one does not purify himself [c5]. And as for the one who came to the one addressed striving, and he fears, the one addressed is distracted from him [c6].
chapters.deep_md: The passage begins by speaking of someone who frowned and turned away, and goes on to speak directly to the one addressed [c1][c2]. It sets one person beside another: one who considers himself in no need and is attended to, and one who came striving and fearing and is not [c4][c6]. It names the possible benefit to the blind man as purifying himself and being reminded [c2][c3], and says what is not upon the one addressed [c5].
chapters.kids_md: The passage tells of a blind man who came, and of someone who frowned and turned away [c1]. It says that the blind man might have been reminded, and that the reminder would have helped him [c3]. It speaks of the one who came striving and fearing [c6].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage turns attention toward the one who comes striving and fearing [c6]. Another is that it sets the one who considers himself in need of nothing beside the one who comes seeking [c4][c6].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: who the blind man is. The verses say only 'the blind man' and give no name.
- Not established: who frowned and turned away. The first verses use a verb with 'he', and the verses that follow speak to 'you'; that they are the same person is an inference from the change of address, and the draft does not state it.
- Not established: who the one is who considers himself in no need, where this took place, or when.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the name of the blind man, the identity of the one who frowned and the occasion. None is used in the story texts, and this draft names no one.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated reports on the occasion of these ayat, on the identity of the blind man and on who is addressed, each with a named grader. None is used in this draft.

The verses do not say that the one who frowned and the one addressed are the same; the inventory title reads them so. A scholar should decide how the page words this, and whether it should name anyone.
The Arabic verb rendered 'purify himself' and the verb rendered 'be reminded' are kept close to the Arabic; their fuller sense is for the reviewer.
Arabic and Urdu texts are not written; they are left null for translators.
